title: Choose the visual world for your portfolio
question: The roll assigned the Asakusa stamp book. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Goshuin Book
options.lineage: 御朱印帳 — the accordion stamp book pilgrims carry to Sensō-ji, every temple stamping a page in vermilion and brush ink
options.thesis: Your career as a pilgrim's stamp book: each shipped product is a page stamped with a vermilion seal, a brush title and the date it went live — the book opens on Soul Bound and Velora.
options.viewport: The book lies open across the whole viewport on its indigo brocade ground: left page Soul Bound, right page Velora, each with a real screenshot set into the page like a pasted print, a vermilion seal SVG stamped over the corner, the title in brush script, the live date hand-written, and 'App Store' as the stamp's inscription. A paper title-slip top-left carries your name; three small index tabs (About · Projects · Skills) stick out of the top edge. Scrolling folds the next spread open.
options.risk: Japanese material on a developer portfolio can read as costume to a recruiter outside Japan; it only holds if every page is a real shipped thing and the stamps are earned, not decorative.

raised.raise: Display titles are brush-made with total commitment — a real brush face and hand-drawn seal strokes, never a sans pretending.
The unstamped page is designed as deliberately as a stamped one: Ivy's 'coming soon' is an empty page with the seal outline waiting, not a greyed card.
No boxes, rules or dividers anywhere — grouping is the fold, the page edge and depth, and the whole book runs past the viewport edges.
The spreads run in time order like named cue phases: 2024 bootcamp pages, 2025 production tools, 2026 App Store — the book reads as chronology, not a grid.

options.label: Tokyo Transit Wayfinding
options.lineage: JR / Metro station signage — line colours, station numbering, bilingual sans, pictograms
options.thesis: Your work laid out as one transit line: each project a numbered station, the two App Store apps the terminals, skills as the line colours — read in two seconds by anyone who has been in Tokyo.
options.viewport: A horizontal line map across the viewport, stations numbered A01–A12 with Soul Bound and Velora as the two large terminal stations, your name on the station board top-left, and the CV as the ticket.
options.risk: Familiar: the structured wayfinding portfolio is where many runs in this category land, and it is quieter than the stamp book.

options.label: Fashion Mook Spread
options.lineage: Japanese fashion mook — coordinate photographs shingled across a spread with hand-drawn annotation ribbons
options.thesis: Screenshots of every app shingled across the spread, each with a hand-drawn ribbon naming the stack and the feature — the project list as a magazine of outfits.
options.viewport: Six overlapping app screenshots across the first viewport, ribbons curling out of each naming it, the active one pulled forward.
options.case: Fuses well — screenshots and annotations are exactly what a portfolio has; holds product clarity, loses audience identification (lace and lolita grammar don't belong to a Rails/iOS developer).
options.risk: The shingle hides half of every screenshot until hovered; recruiters on phones never hover.

options.label: Wuxia Painted Hoarding
options.lineage: painted martial-arts film hoarding, brush title stacked vertically
options.thesis: You as the swordsman mid-leap, projects billed in a hand-lettered band at the foot.
options.viewport: One held frame: figure leaping across the upper two thirds, the title painted down the right edge.
options.case: Loses both axes — a hero portrait of a developer is the thing recruiters trust least, and the billing band flattens twelve projects into a cast list.
options.kept: Brush-made display type with total commitment.
options.risk: Pure poster; nothing on it works as a page.

options.label: Seven-Segment Display
options.lineage: alarm clocks, price totems, scoreboards — one eight-cell mask, unlit segments designed too
options.thesis: The portfolio as a scoreboard: apps shipped, users, years, every number in lit segments.
options.viewport: Four giant red digits counting shipped products, the rest of the page in ghost cells.
options.case: Loses both — it needs numbers to brag with and you have none you may invent; a scoreboard with small honest numbers reads as a loss.
options.kept: Absence drawn as deliberately as presence — the empty page for unshipped work.
options.risk: Retro novelty by the second screen.

options.label: Cathode Numeral Stack
options.lineage: nixie decade counter — every value present as a dark ghost, one struck forward in orange
options.thesis: All twelve projects present as ghosts behind a bronze gauze, one struck forward at a time.
options.viewport: A single struck project glowing orange over eleven unlit sisters in the same glass.
options.case: Loses both — one project visible at a time is the opposite of what a skimming recruiter needs, and the nixie world belongs to no part of your story.
options.kept: No boxes or dividers: grouping by depth alone.
options.risk: Beautiful and unreadable at a glance.

options.label: Cyclorama Dawn
options.lineage: theatre cyc lighting — black through cobalt and rose into white day
options.thesis: Your career as a dawn cue sheet: bootcamp in the dark band, App Store apps in full day.
options.viewport: Horizontal horizon bands stacked dark to light, projects placed on their band.
options.case: Loses both — the gradient-band page is the AI-portfolio default in new clothes, and theatre lighting is nobody's world here.
options.kept: Named phases in time order — the book reads as chronology.

options.label: Sleeping City Fold
options.lineage: surreal folded night city, districts dreaming different weather
options.thesis: Tokyo folded like a quilt, each district a project dreaming its own weather.
options.viewport: A folded map of Tokyo with glowing districts.
options.case: Loses both — a deformable illustrated city is weeks of art you don't have, and it says nothing about shipping software.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dark developer portfolio: name and role hero, avatar, a grid of project cards with stack chips and Live/GitHub buttons, a skills section — executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Centred name and role over an avatar, cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other bootcamp portfolio by design.
